seo.meta_title: 맨정신 Meaning | The Korean 맨- Prefix in BIGBANG's Sober
seo.meta_description: AI confuses the prefix 맨- (bare, nothing added) with 맨 (the very) and 맨날 (always). Learn 맨정신, 맨발, 맨손 and 맨밥.

ai_failure.situation: You see 맨정신, 맨 앞 and 맨날 in the same chat and ask AI what 맨 means.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Gives one meaning for all three, or translates 맨정신 as 'man's mind'.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: These are different 맨s. The prefix 맨- means 'bare, with nothing added': 맨정신 is a sober mind, with no alcohol. 맨 앞 uses a separate word meaning 'the very' (the very front), and 맨날 is spoken Korean for 'every day, always'. BIGBANG's 2015 song 맨정신 (English title 'Sober') uses the prefix form.

natural_solution.rule: 맨 attached to a noun (맨발, 맨손) = bare. 맨 before a position (맨 앞, 맨 위) = the very. 맨날 = always.

alternatives.context: 'I can't do it sober' — e.g. karaoke
Bare feet / bare hands / plain rice with nothing on it
'I'll sit at the very front' — a different 맨

nuance: 맨얼굴 (a face without makeup) is common in beauty talk, though 생얼 is the more casual slang. In spelling, prefix 맨- is attached to the noun (맨발) while 맨 meaning 'the very' is written with a space (맨 앞).
